This approach would be to build a modular fully self-buoyant OTEC system that could be connected to the side of an existing platform. In effect, the OTEC system would add another generator to the platforms power generation system. The conceptual design was described briefly in the 2012 OTC paper “Renewables – Ready or Not?” (Noel and Davis 2012). The design includes a neutrally buoyant hull column containing all of the necessary process and electrical equipment as well as the water inlet piping for the OTEC. The OTEC module would be secured to the side of a floating structure, and the only other connection would be the power cables. One cable is necessary to provide lighting, ventilation, and start-up power to the OTEC system. A second cable enables the net OTEC power to be provided to the platform’s electrical grid. One disadvantage of this approach is the added cost of the self-buoyant hull column, which would not be necessary on a newly designed facility that includes the OTEC system integrated into a hull column. 4.2 Integrated Configurations As discussed in the Objective 2 report, there are several options for integrating an OTEC plant with semi-submersible production facilities. A simplified diagram of a typical semi- submersible platform is shown in Figure 1. Semi submersibles have proven to be an efficient, stable, and safe production platform design. They are also the most popular design among the newly deployed facilities in the GOA2 and are the most likely platform type for future production hub developments.
